messages:
OpsBot: incident created (gpu-pool-exhaustion-usw2) — high GPU queue growth in us-west2, autoscaler errors detected, paging oncall
PagerDuty: page sent to Priya Rao (oncall-sre) and Alex Kim (secondary) :rotating_light:
Priya Rao: I'm on it, joining bridge now — creating short bridge + recording. tagging #customers-impacted if any reports come in
Alex Kim: standing by as second oncall, pulling metrics
Marcus Li: observed queue for model-inference-prod jumped 180 -> 1.2k over 9m, p50 latency spiked 35ms->1.8s, tail 95/99 high. Autoscaler logs show repeated "scale_up_failed: quotaExceeded" errors and then crash-looping with NPE
Tara Singh: Support reports ACME corp seeing 503s and long tail latencies, opened ticket INC-4021. Marking customers impacted: ACME, Skylark.ai
Priya Rao: running quick check: `kubectl get pods -n inference -l app=autoscaler -o yaml` and `gcloud compute regions describe us-west2 --project=redwood-prod`
Marcus Li: paste logs from autoscaler: ```
2025-11-07T21:03:14Z autoscaler ERROR scale_up_failed: compute.regions.quotaExceeded GPUs 0->10 attempted
2025-11-07T21:03:15Z autoscaler ERROR runtime panic: nil pointer deref
2025-11-07T21:03:16Z autoscaler INFO restarting backoff
```
Priya Rao: tried manual scale `kubectl scale --replicas=10 deploy/gpu-worker-usw2 -n inference` -> pods pending with message `0/10 nodes are available: 10 Insufficient nvidia-tesla-t4`
Alex Kim: tried `gcloud compute instances create-from-machine-image` alternative, got: ```
ERROR: Quota 'GPUS' exceeded. Limit: 64. In use: 64.```
So regional GPU quota is saturated.
Marcus Li: interesting — fallback capacity policy was supposed to route to a reserved hot-pool in us-west1 if us-west2 is constrained. Checking routing policy config...
Marcus Li: `redwood-routing` config shows fallback pool label = `gpu-pool: reserved-usw2` but actual reserved pool label on nodes is `gpu-pool: reserved-us-west-2` (suffix mismatch). routing selector failed match -> requests continued hitting exhausted pool
Priya Rao: that explains why fallback didn't kick in. who changed labels? last deploy logs show a tags normalization patch earlier today by infra team (MR #5127) that transformed `usw2` -> `us-west-2` without updating router template
Tara Singh: summary for customers: regional capacity exhausted, autoscaler tried to scale but hit provider GPU quota, fallback routing mislabelled so fallback pool didn't accept traffic, resulted in queue growth and 503s for a subset of heavy-model customers
Priya Rao: mitigation plan: (1) quick rollback of router config to match pool labels (2) manually create 6 on-demand nodes in us-west1 as emergency capacity (3) bump autoscaler image to include guard for quota error to avoid crash-loop
Alex Kim: I'm patching router now — applying `kubectl apply -f` with corrected selector (old value `reserved-usw2`) -> result: `configmap/redwood-routing configured`
SRE Runbook Bot: automated check: verifying pool label match... FAILED -> expected `reserved-usw2` on nodepool but found `reserved-us-west-2` -> runbook step: tag nodes with alias or update selector.
Marcus Li: manual node tag to alias using gcloud instance-templates patch on the reserved pool, letting router match. Command used: ```
gcloud compute instances update t-photos-01 --metadata gpu-pool=reserved-usw2 --zone us-west1-b
```
Priya Rao: meanwhile I requested quota increase via GCP console but that takes time. created support case SR-88922 and escalation to account team.
Alex Kim: spun up 6 temporary on-demand nodes in us-west1 and registered them with the pool. Verified kube nodes Ready and pods scheduled. Running `kubectl get pods -n inference -o wide | grep Pending` -> now 2 pending left, previously 180
Marcus Li: updated autoscaler to skip scaling action on quotaExceeded errors (hotfix image redwood/autoscaler:20251107-hotfix) and restarted deploy. autoscaler no longer crash-looping.
Tara Singh: customer-facing note drafted and pushed to status page: "Partial degradation for inference in us-west2 — mitigation in progress, some customers seeing increased errors/latency" link: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-4021
Priya Rao: monitoring: queue depth dropping 1.2k -> 120 over 22m, 5xx rate for affected customers down to baseline. Marking incident as mitigated, will keep alerts for 30m of stable metrics
Alex Kim: double-check: autoscaler metrics show no more panic but we need a postmortem and automated test to validate label/selector mismatch before prod rollout
Marcus Li: opened follow-up tickets: INFRA-777 (validate routing selectors in CI), QUOTA-221 (request long-term GPU quota increase), RUNBOOK-55 (add explicit check for fallback pool match).
Priya Rao: good catches everyone. postmortem: priority P1 writeup assigned to Marcus Li, due EOD tomorrow. We'll also schedule a runbook walkthrough with infra.
OpsBot: incident status changed to MITIGATED by Priya Rao — monitoring window started. :white_check_mark:
PagerDuty: un-paging Priya Rao and Alex Kim.
Tara Singh: closing customer ticket update: ACME confirmed errors back to normal, will monitor and reopen if they see regressions.
Priya Rao: postmortem/retrospective to include timeline, root cause (quota saturation + label mismatch due to normalization MR), mitigations applied, and concrete preventative actions. Adding `runbook-check` to CI gating for router MR's. :memo:
SRE Runbook Bot: follow-up reminder scheduled in 24h to ensure tags normalization fix propagated across clusters.
Alex Kim: thanks team — nice coordination. :thumbsup:
